I couldn't add the voice-over without changing your video, so I stopped before spending any credits.

**What blocked it:** None of the tools I have can put a new audio track onto an existing video and leave the picture alone.
- The production tool that adds narration only works with clips it generates itself. Its plan would have regenerated your clip as a new AI video (504 credits in total), so the framing and sequence wouldn't stay the same.
- I tested whether its joining step would take your original file directly. It refused (Magic Hour returned "Not Found"), because it only accepts videos it made.
- The other video tools either regenerate the picture (the video editor) or change mouth movements (lip sync), which you didn't want. The tool that joins videos only places them one after another, so it can't lay audio over your clip.

**Options:**
1. **I make the narration and you add it yourself (my suggestion).** I generate a narration-only clip: a plain black screen with a warm, clear English voice reading your script once, no music, about 11 seconds. That costs about 264 credits. You then put its audio under your original clip in any basic editor (CapCut, iMovie, Clipchamp, Premiere and so on), and your video stays exactly as it is. Two caveats:
   - An AI video model speaks the lines, so I can't promise every word comes out exactly right. I'll check it before sending it to you.

2. **Regenerate the video with a voice.** This gives you one finished file, but the picture would be a new AI version of your clip, not the original. That goes against your "keep the video unchanged" request, so I don't recommend it.
3. **You record or supply the audio.** If you have a voice file you'd prefer, you can still add it the same way as in option 1.

Should I go ahead with option 1?
